stories.title: US Air Force pulls bombers from UK air base after suspected terror attack
stories.summary: The US Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a US-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base. The bombers were redeployed back to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorized to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke Sunday on condition of anonymity. Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers fly out of the base on Sunday. The move comes as President Donald Trump weighs options for his war on Iran - including new strikes - despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks. "We have decisions that I'll make about Iran. Iran's been decimated. So the only question is - it'll either be the easy way, or the hard way,"

stories.title: India seeks bigger role in effort to end the Russia-Ukraine War

article_sentences: India is taking a more direct role in efforts to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, engaging both sides on issues, including shipping and reducing hostilities, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said.

Speaking at a security conference over the weekend, Jaishankar said India in recent months has become “a little bit more involved beyond advocacy.” The comments point to a more active role for New Delhi after years of taking a cautious approach to the war, in part because of its longstanding ties with Russia.
“We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.
We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” he said, adding that talks have also covered energy shipments and “non-attack possibilities.”
India has called for a halt to the fighting but has been reluctant to criticize the Kremlin, abstaining from United Nations votes condemning the war.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the conflict during a meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan in late August.
Jaishankar said dialogue and diplomacy are essential to ending the war.
He added that India’s relationship with Russia has evolved over the years and now spans energy, space and trade.

When Modi met Putin on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in September, the two pledged to deepen ties, underscoring their close relationship even as Washington pressed New Delhi to distance itself from Moscow.
The US has sought to use its position as India’s top trading partner to pressure New Delhi to stop buying Russian oil.
India’s purchases initially declined before picking up again during the Middle East war.
Russia is also a major supplier of weapons to New Delhi.

stories.headline: Trump cites Indian election that never happened to call US voting 'CORRUPT'
stories.title: Trump cites Indian election that never happened to call US voting 'CORRUPT'
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Trump's reference to India appears to be a mix-up with Brazil, which held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday.

Washington: US President Donald Trump appears to have confused India with Brazil while attacking the American electoral process, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian presidential election that did not take place.

In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump cited what he described as the results of India's "Presidential Election" to argue that US elections take too long to count and are therefore vulnerable to manipulation.
"125 Million People voted today in the first round of India's Presidential Election.
The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY," Trump said.
He then contrasted the alleged Indian process with vote counting in several US cities and states.
"In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate.
Voting in America is CORRUPT," the US president said.
Brazil's electoral authority recorded 125.27 million valid votes in the election.
Results began to be released at 5 pm, when voting ended, and were updated as ballots were received and processed.
The Brazilian election pitted incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.
Neither candidate secured a majority, sending the election to a runoff scheduled for October 25.

stories.title: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
stories.summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot alleged the SIR is being used to selectively delete voters, as he also criticised the Rajasthan government’s drought response and the AAP government in Punjab
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Sunday (October 4, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the independence of the Election Commission, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was being used to selectively delete voters.

Talking to reporters in Jaipur, Mr. Pilot alleged that Mr. Kumar had sidelined the other two Election Commissioners while taking decisions related to the electoral roll revision, and demanded action against him.
“India and the country function according to law.
The Election Commission has three members, and decisions are taken either unanimously or by a majority.
But Gyanesh Kumar sidelined the other two Election Commissioners and started the entire process on his own,” he alleged.
Mr. Pilot claimed that powers normally exercised by Electoral Registration.
Officers (EROs) at the local level were being centralised, and alleged that names of voters were being added or deleted from Delhi.
He claimed about 13 crore names had been removed from electoral rolls across the country, and alleged that voters were being selectively targeted in States including Haryana, Bihar and West Bengal.
“First there was demonetisation, and now they are doing ‘votebandi’.
Voting is the biggest democratic right of a citizen.
If that right is taken away, what could be more serious than this?” Mr. Pilot said.
He alleged that public confidence in the Election Commission as an impartial constitutional institution had been eroded, and demanded action against the CEC.

article_sentences: The Chief Justice commented that the Court will not indulge in a mere academic exercise.

The Supreme Court's 7-judge reference on the issue of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech might be disposed of as an academic issue, since the Court was informed today that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly, which was the trigger for the case, was withdrawn in 2004.
The reference originates from the 2003 case N. Ravi.
Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai, challenging the 2003 decision taken by the Tamil Nadu assembly to sentence 5 journalists of The Hindu for articles criticising the State Government.
The matter was ultimately referred to the 7-judge bench to examine the interplay between Articles 194(3), 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution.
The reference remained pending for over two decades, and the Court, in August 2026, decided to commence the hearing from October 6.

A day before the scheduled hearing of the reference, Senior Advocate Raju Ramachandran, for the State of Tamil Nadu, today informed a 3-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant that the 2003 resolution of the Assembly was revoked in 2004 itself.
Though an affidavit was filed in the Court regarding this development, this fact was omitted to be noticed in the reference order.
Since the cause of action for the case no longer survives, the reference may have become academic, Ramachandran suggested.
Ramachandran said that he was making this mention today so that the 7-judge bench is not taken by surprise tomorrow.
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta also said that the issue may have become academic in the light of this information.
The Chief Justice expressed that the Court will not indulge in a mere academic exercise.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 5 : The Supreme Court will hear petitions on Monday challenging whether Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar can single-handedly exercise powers constitutionally designated for the entire multi-member poll panel. As per the cause list published on the official website of the apex court, a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is slated to take up the matter. The matter was mentioned before the CJI earlier on September 29 by senior advocate Vikas Singh, following which the CJI said: "List it next week." The plea seeks enforcement of the collective decision-making framework governing the ECI and a writ in the nature of quo warranto concerning the authority under which the CEC has reportedly acted in the name of the poll panel. The petition contends that Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the “Commission” and not in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It further relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which provides for collective decision-making, with matters on which there is no unanimity to be decided by majority. The plea has relied upon contemporaneous written communications and file notings attributed to Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who allegedly recorded at least 14 objections between October 2025 and August 2026 concerning decisions and steps allegedly taken in the name of the ECI without their approval. The objections, as detailed in the petition, relate to communications and orders allegedly issued without the poll body's approval, the absence of agendas before and minutes after meetings, foreign travel undertaken without approval, changes to Form 6, access to the electoral roll database and filing of appeals before tribunals in West Bengal. The plea also refers to concerns reportedly raised by the two Election Commissioners over the "gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database", and changes in the work allocation of the poll body's IT establishment. The petitioner has sought a declaration that powers vested in the ECI under Article 324 cannot be exercised or represented as an act of the poll body except in accordance with the constitutional and statutory framework governing the Commission. The plea also seeks declaratory and mandatory directions to ensure compliance with the collective decision-making framework, besides production and preservation of relevant records concerning the disputed decisions. Meanwhile, the ECI has maintained that the reported differences between the Commissioners do not amount to an institutional "rupture" and that internal objections and written notes are established mechanisms in a multi-member constitutional body. --IANS

stories.headline: RBI begins policy meeting as inflation pressures strengthen case for rate hike
stories.title: RBI begins policy meeting as inflation pressures strengthen case for rate hike
stories.summary: The RBI’s three-day policy meeting began on Monday, with a decision on the current 5.25 per cent repo rate due on Wednesday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee began its three-day meeting on Monday amid mounting expectations of an interest rate increase, as rising inflation, higher oil prices and a weakening rupee complicate the policy outlook.
The committee will announce its decision on Wednesday, 7 October.
The benchmark repo rate currently stands at 5.25 per cent, with markets watching for what could be the first increase since February 2023.
Bank of America has brought forward its forecast for a 25-basis-point hike from December to October.
It said higher energy costs, food inflation and price pressures spreading across the economy could prompt the RBI to begin withdrawing monetary support at this meeting.
SBI Research also sees the risks increasingly favouring a quarter-percentage-point increase.
Its report cited broadening inflation, deteriorating global conditions, changes in liquidity and renewed repricing of risk in financial markets as reasons for acting early.
The report argued that a pre-emptive response would be prudent given geopolitical tensions and the threat of further increases in crude prices.
Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July.
Crude oil trading above $100 a barrel, rupee weakness and higher global bond yields have added to the pressures facing policymakers.
The outlook for food prices presents a further concern.
Strong El Niño conditions and the prospect of below-normal rainfall in October could affect rabi crop output, potentially adding to inflation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to list plea to allow peaceful protests to Jantar Mantar
stories.title: Supreme Court to list plea to allow peaceful protests to Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: The petition sought judicial directions from the apex court to the police to allow peaceful protests.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) indicates that it will list a petition alleging that the Delhi.
Police is not allowing peaceful protests and marches to Jantar Mantar in the national capital following allegations of misconduct by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and seeking his removal.
Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, a counsel orally mentioned a petition against the capital’s police.
“The Delhi Police is not allowing students, ordinary citizens, party leaders, MLAs and MPs to peacefully protest,” the counsel submitted.
The petition sought judicial directions from the apex court to the police to allow peaceful protests.
He said the right to peaceful protest was recognised in the Constitution, endorsed by the court, as a fundamental right under Article 19.
“We will list the petition, and then you can argue,” Chief Justice Kant said.
